sensors.name: line tracker brightness in % (floor under it)

functions: followLine (b4): reads the line tracker and sets a curve or a straight drive, then returns

actions.name: curve with left wheel 7 %, right wheel 22 % (curves left)
curve with left wheel 22 %, right wheel 7 % (curves right)

control_flow: followLine: if the line tracker reads below 30 %, curve left; else if it reads above 70 %, curve right; else drive straight on.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line with the line tracker.

decision_points.condition: first: the line tracker reads below 30 %; second: it reads above 70 %

branches.outcome: above 70 % (white band or peach floor): it curves right

branches.reason: Only right at the edge of the line's black core, for a moment.
branches.outcome: between 30 % and 70 %: it drives straight on

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left while the floor reads below 30 %, curves right while it reads above 70 %, and drives straight on in between
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line, facing along it
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees the black line, then the white band beside it, again and again
scenarios.title: Follows the line
assumptions: The end of the line is where it should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end

uncertainties: On black the program curves left, which may steer it further off the line: whether it can follow the line is what the tests show.
The straight-on branch only happens for a moment at the edge of the black core, so it is hard to plan alone.
The line tracker only sees floor brightness: dark tunnels and walls make no difference to it.

planned: On a straight line, it follows it to the goal
On a curved line, it follows it to the goal

outcomes.words: condition 2 holds (the ones before it don't)
